import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 951

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/951](https://www.erdosproblems.com/951)
 - [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ.,
    New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
-/

open scoped Finsupp Nat.Prime Topology
open Filter

namespace Erdos951

/-- A sequence `a : ℕ → ℝ` is said to have property `Erdos951Prop` if for any pair of distinct
finitely supported sequences `k l : ℕ →₀ ℕ` their corresponding Beurling integers are of distance
at least one apart. -/
def Erdos951Prop (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (k ℓ : ℕ →₀ ℕ), k ≠ ℓ → |beurlingInteger a k - beurlingInteger a ℓ| ≥ 1

/-- If `a` has property `Erdos951Prop` and `1 < a 0`, then `a` is a set of Beurling
prime numbers. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951.variants.isBeurlingPrimes {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : 1 < a 0)
    (hm : StrictMono a) (he : Erdos951Prop a) :
    IsBeurlingPrimes a := by
  refine ⟨ha, hm, tendsto_atTop_atTop.2 fun x => ?_⟩
  by_contra h_contra
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ : ∃ L, Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop (𝓝 L) :=
    ⟨_, tendsto_atTop_isLUB hm.monotone (isLUB_ciSup ⟨x, Set.forall_mem_range.2 fun n =>
    le_of_not_ge fun hn => h_contra ⟨n, fun m hm' => hn.trans (hm.monotone hm')⟩⟩)⟩
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := Metric.tendsto_atTop.mp hL (1 / 2) (by norm_num)
  have := hm (by linarith : N < N + 1)
  have h_diff : a (N + 1) - a N ≥ 1 := by
    rw [← abs_of_nonneg (by linarith : 0 ≤ a _ - _)]
    simpa using he (.single (N + 1) 1) (.single N 1) (by simpa [Finsupp.ext_iff] using ⟨N, by simp⟩)
  linarith [abs_lt.1 (hN N le_rfl), abs_lt.1 (hN (N + 1) (by grind))]

/-- If `1 < a 0 < ...` has property `Erdos951Prop`, is it true that `#{a i ≤ x} ≤ π x`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, 1 < a 0 → StrictMono a → Erdos951Prop a →
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, {i : ℕ | a i ≤ x}.ncard ≤ π ⌊x⌋₊ := by
  sorry

/-- Beurling conjectured that if the number of Beurling integer in `[1, x]`
is `x + o(log x)`, then `a` must be the sequence of primes. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951.variants.beurling :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, IsBeurlingPrimes a →
    ((fun x => (BeurlingIntegers a ∩ .Iic x).ncard - x) =o[atTop] Real.log) →
    a = Nat.cast ∘ Nat.nth Nat.Prime := by
  sorry

end Erdos951

findings.description: The counting function on line 69 discards multiplicities: `BeurlingIntegers a` is `Set.range (beurlingInteger a)`. However, `IsBeurlingPrimes a` only requires positivity, strict increase, and divergence; it does not make different exponent tuples produce different values. Consequently the statement is false for `a n = (n : ℝ) + 2`. This sequence satisfies `IsBeurlingPrimes`, its set of product values is precisely the positive integers, and its counting function is therefore `⌊x⌋₊ = x + O(1) = x + o(log x)`. Nevertheless, `a 2 = 4`, whereas the third prime is 5. A complete Lean proof of the negation of this variant is in `/workspace/review/counterexample.lean`; its axioms contain no `sorryAx`.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, [Er77c], pp. 68–69 (https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-27.pdf), states Beurling's conjecture immediately after the separated-product problem. The current problem page likewise refers to 'such a sequence'. For general Beurling systems, the standard counting convention explicitly preserves multiplicities: Hilberdink–Lapidus, §1.1, equations (1.1)–(1.2), says sums count multiplicities, 'Similarly for [the sum over generalized integers]' (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0410270). Lagarias, §1, explicitly treats different power products as distinct (https://dept.math.lsa.umich.edu/~lagarias/doc/beurling.ps). The Lean declaration neither preserves these multiplicities nor retains the source context's separation hypothesis.
findings.suggested_fix: For the general Beurling conjecture, replace the counting function by the count of exponent tuples: `fun x : ℝ => ({k : ℕ →₀ ℕ | beurlingInteger a k ≤ x}.ncard : ℝ) - x`. If the intended declaration is specifically the variant for the one-separated sequences in the Erdős problem, retain `Erdos951Prop a` as an explicit hypothesis instead; under that hypothesis the product map is injective and set counting agrees with counting tuples. Clarify which version is intended in the docstring.

findings.description: The docstring says that `Erdos951Prop a` and `1 < a 0` suffice for `IsBeurlingPrimes a`, but the theorem also requires `hm : StrictMono a`. That hypothesis is not redundant: the sequence 3, 2, 5, 7, ... satisfies the two documented hypotheses by unique factorization, but is not strictly increasing and therefore fails the repository's definition of `IsBeurlingPrimes`. The Lean theorem itself correctly includes the hypothesis.
findings.source_evidence: The source begins with a strictly increasing sequence, 'Let 1 < a₁ < ⋯' (https://www.erdosproblems.com/951; [Er77c], p. 68). Lines 39–40 of the reviewed file omit this assumption from the API lemma's docstring, while lines 42–43 include it in Lean.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'strictly increasing' to the docstring's assumptions, for example: 'If `a` is strictly increasing, has property `Erdos951Prop`, and satisfies `1 < a 0`, then `a` is a sequence of Beurling primes.'

reformulations.difference: The statement does not separately assume divergence to infinity and counts generator indices rather than distinct generator values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The separation property applied to consecutive singleton exponent tuples gives successive generator gaps at least 1, so strict increase and separation force divergence to infinity. The counted index set is therefore finite. Strict monotonicity makes the generator map injective, so its index count equals the cardinality of `Set.range a ∩ Set.Iic x`. `/workspace/review/reformulations.lean` proves the equivalence between the displayed generator assumptions and `IsBeurlingPrimes a ∧ Erdos951Prop a`, and proves equality of the two counts. `/workspace/review/boundaries.lean` verifies finiteness.

reformulations.difference: The counting interval is implemented with `Set.Iic x`, although the source specifies `[1,x]`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under `IsBeurlingPrimes a`, every generator is greater than 1, so every finite product of nonnegative powers is at least 1, including the empty product, which equals 1. Thus `BeurlingIntegers a ∩ Set.Iic x` equals `BeurlingIntegers a ∩ Set.Icc 1 x` for every real x. Both this equality and the resulting little-o equivalence are proved in `/workspace/review/reformulations.lean`. This is independent of the multiplicity defect.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/951 — complete statement, remarks, and current status; retrieved through r.jina.ai after direct requests returned a Cloudflare challenge.
https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/951 — mathematical discussion of the all-x versus eventual interpretations, especially the January 2026 comments by Bloom and Tao.
Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III (1977), pp. 68–69: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-27.pdf
Hilberdink–Lapidus, Beurling Zeta Functions, Generalised Primes, and Fractal Membranes, §1.1; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0410270
Lagarias, Beurling generalized integers with the Delone property, §1 and introductory results: https://dept.math.lsa.umich.edu/~lagarias/doc/beurling.ps
Lagarias's publication pages, used to locate the paper: https://dept.math.lsa.umich.edu/~lagarias/publications.html and https://dept.math.lsa.umich.edu/~lagarias/zeta.html

Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/NumberTheory/BeurlingPrimes.lean; Mathlib definitions of Finsupp.prod, Set.ncard, Nat.primeCounting, Nat.nth, Nat.floor, Real.log, and Asymptotics.IsLittleO.
review.notes: All four declarations were checked. The main theorem selects the eventual-in-x interpretation expressly contemplated by the source; the recorded finite counterexample at x = 10 does not refute that interpretation, and its `research open` tag matches the current source. The consulted sources do not establish a settlement of the separate Beurling conjecture, so I could not corroborate its `research solved` tag; absence of a cited settlement is not reported as a confirmed status issue. All experiments were confined to /workspace/review/, and the reviewed file matches its committed hash.

submission.summary: Changed the Beurling variant to count finitely supported exponent tuples, preserving multiplicities, and clarified this convention in its docstring. Also corrected the API lemma's docstring to include its strict-monotonicity hypothesis. Only 951.lean was edited. The required compile command succeeds with only the permitted `declaration uses sorry` warnings.
